decisive_items: A 36-year-old woman with a 17-year history of migraine headaches
characterized by a visual aura of gray-white spots followed by pain behind the right eye
She typically had 3 to 4 severe migraines per month lasting 3 to 7 days
response.rationale: Long-standing migraine with aura and frequent severe episodes meeting chronic migraine criteria; new headache features are not accompanied by autonomic signs or short-lasting attacks, making trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia less specific.

rejected.why: Treatment failure is not a diagnosis.
Lacks autonomic features and episodic short-lasting pattern typical of cluster headache.
No indomethacin response or continuous unremitting pattern clearly documented.
Pain is continuous, not paroxysmal electric-shock like.
No explicit medication overuse frequency or withdrawal pattern.
